claims.text: What the strip looks like A wide QRS @ 20–40 w ⍉P waves.
claims.quote: Idioventricular rhythm: Wide QRS, rate 20–40, no P waves.
Ventricular Escape Rhythm: A ventricular rhythm with a rate of 20-40 bpm.

claims.text: QRS: broad (≥ 120 ms), may look like LBBB or RBBB
claims.quote: QRS complexes are broad (≥ 120 ms) and may have a LBBB or RBBB morphology.

claims.text: AIVR: regular, typically 50–120, three or more ventricular complexes w QRS > 120 ms, fusion and capture beats
claims.quote: Regular rhythm Rate typically 50-120 bpm Three or more ventricular complexes; QRS duration > 120ms Fusion and capture beats

claims.text: Rate tells them apart: < 50 fits a ventricular escape rhythm; > 110 fits VT
claims.quote: Rates < 50 bpm are consistent with a Ventricular Escape Rhythm Rates > 110 bpm are consistent with Ventricular Tachycardia

claims.text: Isorhythmic AV dissociation: sinus and ventricular complexes @ identical rates
claims.quote: This refers to AV dissociation with sinus and ventricular complexes occurring at identical rates.

claims.text: → (mech and diagnoses) Escape mech: a ventricular pacemaker takes over when the supraventricular impulses reaching the ventricle are slower than its own intrinsic rate
claims.quote: Junctional and ventricular escape rhythms arise when the rate of supraventricular impulses arriving at the AV node or ventricle is less than the intrinsic rate of the ectopic pacemaker.

claims.text: Escape Eti: severe sinus brady, sinus arrest, SA exit block, high-grade second-degree or third-degree AV block, hyperkalemia, BB, calcium-channel-blocker or digoxin poisoning
claims.quote: Severe sinus bradycardia Sinus arrest Sino-atrial exit block High-grade second degree AV block Third degree AV block Hyperkalaemia Drugs: beta-blocker, calcium-channel blocker or digoxin poisoning

claims.text: AIVR mech: an ectopic ventricular pacemaker outpaces the sinus node, often w ↑vagal and ↓sympathetic tone
claims.quote: AIVR, also known as Accelerated Ventricular Rhythm, results when the rate of an ectopic ventricular pacemaker exceeds that of the sinus node. Often associated with increased vagal tone and decreased sympathetic tone.

claims.text: AIVR Eti: reperfusion after acute MI (MC); beta-sympathomimetics (isoprenaline, adrenaline); drug toxicity (digoxin, cocaine, desflurane); lyte abnormalities; cardiomyopathy, congenital Hdz, myocarditis; return of circ after arrest; athletic ♡
claims.quote: Reperfusion phase of acute myocardial infarction (MI) — most common cause Beta-sympathomimetics such as isoprenaline or adrenaline Drug toxicity, especially digoxin, cocaine and volatile anaesthetics such as desflurane Electrolyte abnormalities Cardiomyopathy, congenital heart disease, myocarditis Return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) following cardiac arrest — this probably relates to reperfusion of acute MI as underlying cause of arrest Athletic heart

claims.text: Sx AIVR: USU well tolerated, benign and self-limiting
claims.quote: Usually a well-tolerated, benign, self-limiting arrhythmia

claims.text: Tx AIVR: USU benign and ⍉treated unless there are hemodynamic Sx
claims.quote: Repetitive ventricular rhythms at slower rates are called accelerated idioventricular rhythms or slow VT; they are usually benign and are not treated unless patients have hemodynamic symptoms.

claims.text: It USU resolves on its own once the sinus rate exceeds the ventricular focus
claims.quote: AIVR is a benign rhythm in most settings and does not usually require treatment Usually self limiting and resolves when sinus rate exceeds that of the ventricular foci

claims.text: ⍉antiarrhythmics — they may cause sudden hemodynamic deterioration; tx the cause (correct lytes, restore myocard perf)
claims.quote: Administration of anti-arrhythmics may cause precipitous haemodynamic deterioration and should be avoided Treat the underlying cause: e.g. correct electrolytes, restore myocardial perfusion

claims.text: ↓CO states: atropine may be tried to speed the sinus rate and restore AV synchrony (atrial kick)
claims.quote: Patients with low cardiac output states (e.g. severe biventricular failure) may benefit from restoration of AV synchrony to restore atrial kick – in this case atropine may be trialed in an attempt to increase sinus rate and AV conduction

LITFL gives AIVR a typical rate of 50–120.
LITFL counts rates under 50 as a ventricular escape rhythm.
claims.quote: Rates < 50 bpm are consistent with a Ventricular Escape Rhythm
